previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and left shoulder pain following a fall. She had recently completed treatment for C. diff and presented with a recurrence, confirmed by a positive stool toxin test. She was started on high-dose oral vancomycin, with gradual improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms. During admission, she was found to have acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, evidenced by pulmonary edema on chest imaging, which improved with IV and oral diuretics. She developed transient worsening of renal function, likely due to fluid overload, which stabilized with diuresis. A transfusion of one unit of packed red blood cells was given for symptomatic anemia, with good response. Chest pain was evaluated and attributed to a combination of heart failure, GERD, and abdominal inflammation, rather than acute coronary syndrome. She remained DNR/DNI throughout. At discharge, she was stable, transitioning to extended care with a plan to continue vancomycin under Infectious Disease guidance and monitor fluid status closely.

INDICATION:  ___ female with coronary artery disease and chronic renal
failure, abdominal pain.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  Helical MDCT images were acquired from the lung bases through the
greater trochanters without intravenous contrast, due to the patient's chronic
renal failure.  Oral contrast was not administered.  Coronal and sagittal
multiplanar reformations were generated.

contrast, body habitus, and patient motion.

Mild atelectasis is noted at the lung bases.  There are no pleural effusions.

There is mild surrounding fat stranding and fascial thickening, but no
evidence of drainable fluid collections.  There is no evidence of osseous
destruction to suggest superinfection.

ABDOMEN:  The liver, gallbladder, pancreas, and spleen are unremarkable on
this non-contrast examination.  The left adrenal is slightly full, without
definite nodularity.  The right adrenal is normal.  The kidneys are slightly
atrophic, with cortical thinning and lobulation reflecting prior infectious or
ischemic injury.  There are no renal stones or hydronephrosis.

The stomach is normal.  Note is made of a diverticulum arising from the second
portion of the duodenum.  The remainder of the small bowel is normal.

PELVIS:  The colon and rectum are unremarkable.  The bladder and distal
ureters are normal.  The uterus has bulky appearance with multiple dystrophic
calcifications, suggesting underlying fibroids.  There is no free
intraperitoneal air.

Coarse calcifications are noted throughout the abdominal aorta and iliac
arteries, with mild stenosis of the celiac and superior mesenteric artery
origins.  Retroperitoneal and mesenteric lymph nodes are not pathologically
enlarged.

The bones are diffusely demineralized.  There is straightening of the normal
lumbar lordosis, with bridging osteophytes noted at T9-10.  No suspicious
lytic or sclerotic osseous lesions are identified.

Diffuse body wall edema is noted.

1.  No acute abdominal process.
2.  Fibroid uterus.
3.  Small hiatal hernia.

INDICATION:  ___ female with painful swollen left lower extremity. 
Evaluate for DVT.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  Gray-scale and color sonographic imaging of the left common
femoral, superficial femoral, and popliteal veins was performed.  Evaluation
of the distal superficial femoral vein was slightly limited due to body
habitus, and color flow only seen in the calf veins.  Elsewhere, the veins
demonstrate normal flow, augmentation, and compressibility.  There is no
echogenic intraluminal thrombus identified.  Symmetric respiratory phasicity
was seen in the contralateral common femoral vein.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of left lower extremity DVT.

INDICATION:  ___ female with chronic kidney disease, being evaluated
prior to AV fistula placement.

TECHNIQUE AND FINDINGS:  The veins in the upper extremity were evaluated with
B-mode ultrasound.

The arteries in the upper extremities were evaluated with color and spectral
Doppler ultrasound.

FINDINGS:  On the right side, the right cephalic vein is patent and
compressible with diameters ranging between 0.12 and 0.23 cm.  The right
basilic vein is patent and compressible with diameters ranging between 0.1 and
0.28 cm.  The right brachial artery is duplicated, and presents patent with
triphasic Doppler waveforms.

On the left side, the left cephalic vein is patent and compressible with
diameters ranging between 0.06 and 0.27 cm.  The left basilic vein is patent
and compressible with diameters ranging between 0.18 and 0.29 cm.  The left
brachial artery is duplicated, and presents patent with triphasic Doppler
waveforms.

Both subclavian veins are patent with normal phasicity bilaterally.

COMPARISON:  None available.

IMPRESSION:  Patent subclavian veins bilaterally.

Patent cephalic and basilic veins bilaterally with diameters described as
above.  Patent duplicated brachial arteries bilaterally.
